Definition: from G2294; to have courage:--be of good cheer (comfort). Compare G2292.
BiblicalUsage: tharséō is the word for to have courage, to be of good cheer. In Matthew 9:2, be of good cheer. Wherever it appears, the word means this and not something vaguer.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the Bible does not use this word lightly, and neither should I. That is why tharséō stays with me long after the verse is closed.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
